title: Traffic Inspector: sampled mirroring with tenant sandboxing and cost guardrails
creator: Maya Lopez
description: Introduce a Traffic Inspector service that enables non-disruptive, budget-aware mirroring of production requests for model lifecycle workflows (canary validation, A/B evaluation, offline replay). The Inspector performs tenant-aware sampling, redaction/PII protection, and routes mirrored payloads into isolated sandboxes or ephemeral serving pools. It centralizes cost accounting and exposes admin controls to throttle or pause mirroring per org or project.
background: Current mirroring pipelines are either all-or-nothing or use static sampling knobs. This results in cost spikes, noisy tenant interference, and complicated post-hoc filtering. Teams building canary rollouts and A/B tests need predictable mirroring spend, guaranteed non-interference with production SLAs, and simple controls to quarantine problematic tenants or models.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic Inspector can mirror traffic with a tenant-scoped sampling rate configurable via API and Console
Mirrored payloads are routed to an isolated sandbox namespace that cannot affect production state or bill production resources
Per-tenant credit accounting prevents mirror spend above configured budget; Inspector automatically pauses mirroring for tenants that exceed budget and emits events
An adaptive sampler reduces mirror rate when production latency or GPU utilization crosses safety thresholds
PII redaction rules are applied to mirrored payloads (configurable allowlist/denylist) and verified in tests
Console shows token-level cost estimates for mirrored traffic and historical mirror burn charts
E2E integration test that creates a canary, enables Inspector mirroring at 5% sample, validates mirrored responses land in sandbox and do not impact production latencies
implementation_notes: Introduce Traffic Inspector as an ingress sidecar or gateway layer that can be toggled per route via routing policy
Sampling strategy: hybrid reservoir + rate decay. Default: reservoir sampling for initial burst, then exponential decay to maintain long-term rate
Budgeting: tenant-level credit ledger backed by existing billing DB. Inspector debits credits at mirror enqueue time and supports a soft-limit and hard-cutoff
Isolation: mirrored requests are forwarded into sandbox cluster with network policies, read-only metadata access, and disabled external side-effects (no downstream writes)
Redaction: pluggable transform pipeline (regex + schema-aware) that marks fields for removal or hashing. Must integrate with existing tokenizers to estimate token counts for cost accounting
Backpressure policy: when production latency/queueing breach SLO, the Inspector shifts to aggressive sampling (min of 0.1%) then to full pause if emergency threshold hit
Control plane: expose REST endpoints and Console feature flag for per-tenant mirroring toggles, budgets, sampling profiles, and emergency circuit breakers
Metrics/events: mirror_enqueue, mirror_drop_reason, mirror_cost_debit, mirror_pause_event, sampler_rate_per_tenant
Security: require security review before enabling redaction rules; ensure HSM/KMS keys not mirrored; audit logs for mirrored payload access
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit tests + local emulator of sandbox; small internal traffic canary (platform alpha team)
Phase 2 (staged): enable inspector in staging cluster for 10 internal services; validate cost accounting and redaction
Phase 3 (pilot): roll to 5 customer tenants with strict budgets and manual ops approval
Phase 4 (GA): UI controls in Console, auto-budget recommendations from Optimize, default conservative sampling profiles
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling algorithms and edge cases (burst, idle, budget depletion)
Integration tests that assert mirrored requests are isolated and that production SLOs remain unchanged under mirrored load
Chaos test: randomly trigger Inspector pause and resume; verify automatic recovery and ledger correctness
Security test: PII redaction fuzzing and proof that KMS-protected fields are never copied
Load test: simulate 100k TPS ingress with 1% mirror rate; verify cost accounting and enqueue latency
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: mirror_pause_for_tenant when budget exhausted (page on high customer-impact tenants)
Alert: mirror_enqueue_latency > 50ms or mirror_queue_depth > X (safety throttle triggered)
Dashboard: mirror spend by tenant, mirror sampling rate, mirror success/drop breakdown
Trace hooks: tag mirrored spans and correlate with production traces for post-mortem
risks: If redaction rules are incomplete, PII could be mirrored. Mitigation: require conservative denylist-first defaults + security review
Budget accounting drift between Inspector and billing if tokens are estimated differently. Mitigation: align tokenization library and reconcile daily
Sandbox performance could vary from production causing misleading evaluation results. Mitigation: annotate sandbox metrics and surface expected delta in Console
Operator complexity: too many per-tenant knobs could confuse teams. Mitigation: provide sane defaults and an "auto" mode that uses Optimize recommendations
notes: This ticket rethinks mirroring from 'replicate everything then filter' to 'inspect, sample, transform, and isolate' with built-in cost governance. It is purposely conservative: default sampling profiles will be low and admins must opt into aggressive mirroring.
